title: Relief Against a Granite Ridge Restoration Charge for a Season the Holder Has Not Used
content:
| Scans standing on the pass account | Days the pass has been scannable | Share of the charge relieved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none at all | at least 45 | three tenths, a rate of 30 per cent |
| none at all | fewer than 45 | a fifth, a rate of 20 per cent |
| one or more | any number | no relief on this head |

The schedule above governs the relief given against the charge for restoring scanning privileges on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass where the holder has taken no day of the season. Where the pass account shows no scan at all and the pass has been scannable for at least 45 days, three tenths of the charge is relieved. Where the pass account shows no scan at all and the pass has been scannable for fewer than 45 days, a fifth of the charge is relieved. In any other case no relief is given on this head.

Note 1. The figure of 45 days is a count of days since the pass became scannable, not a count of the season's operating days, and the day the pass became scannable is where the count starts. At 44 days the rate is 20 per cent, at 45 it is 30 per cent, and above 45 it does not rise further.

Note 2. A single scan standing on the pass account closes both rows, however long ago it was recorded.

Note 3, worked on a hypothetical account. A Granite Ridge Local Pass became scannable on 1 December and shows no scan at all. On a handling date of 10 January the pass has been scannable for 40 days, so a fifth of the charge is relieved. On a handling date of 15 January it has been scannable for 45 days and three tenths of the charge is relieved instead.
